items.title: Bob Shoffner Interview, 1959-09-08
items.q: Eddie Allen, who knew me before I went in on me, after coming home, he said, why don't you go down and see Charlie Crisp?

ctx.x: And when I came out of the army in 1919, Charlie Crisp was in St. Louis. Well he had set St. Louis on fire. He was working on the boat. And he wanted a trumpet player. Well Eddie Allen, who knew me before I went in on me, after coming home, he said, why don't you go down and see Charlie Crisp? But I said, well I can't play that kind of music. I said, well I know it's just straight legit music. So he said, well you go down and see Charlie. Well I wasn't seeing Charlie. And Charlie had me play the first night on…
Did they use written arrangements in his band or?
